thesis: The speakers describe how WCM Investment Management rebuilt its firm after underperforming for five years and losing $4 billion in assets by launching an international strategy with inexperienced managers and a small portfolio. They argue that relying on conventional wisdom to buy high-quality large-cap companies at a discount leads to average returns because everyone does the same thing, so the firm had to think differently to succeed.
